english: Foxmen love their quests. An overwhelming wanderlust drives them to seek any excuse to go on a grand adventure. The goal is most often entirely beside the point, and often forgotten early in their journeys. Few however are willing to give up the dream of finding true love with one of Tali's most beutiful creations. [PARAGRAPH]Slyphs are beautiful air spirits have been known to give up their eternal dances among the winds and clouds to marry mortal men. The only consistent part of their ephemeral nature if their faithfulness to their spouse, who will invariably be blessed with a happy marriage. But their children, although frequently brilliant and creative, are often restless and troublesome for many generations. Many suspect Tali created the Slyphs specifically to breed this tendency into men.

The Church of Bhall has little long-lasting structure. Instead religious upheavals happen and huge masses of fanatical followers rise up and rebel against whatever is being protested in that area. The cause is less important than the fervor, the blessing of Bhall, and the violence that comes with the rebellion. Most worshipers of Bhall receive a brand of her mark that forever burns and inflicts pain. Bhall is also known as the Queen of Fire and the Fallen Star. [PARAGRAPH]The Sanctus Inquisition was formed after the Second Rebellion, to purge Patria of its corruption. This is a movement devoted to Bhall, full of priests, rioters and inquisitors wielding golden seraphic fire. This Fire could burn demonic flesh and break spells. Basium joined the Sanctus Inquisition and Cassiel built a home for the refugees displaced by the war. Though Kylorin duelled the most powerful of the rebellion's enemies, it was the Sanctus Inquisition that fought a hundred battles around Patria. [PARAGRAPH]During these battles, some of the most devout inquisitioners endured the Ritual of the Smokeless Fire. They knelt and prayed to Bhall, prayed for victory, prayed for the fall of the Imprimatur Council, and offered their life as sacrifice that they protect those they love. Then they set themselves on fire. The truly faithful become possessed by one of the Seven Ifrit, incorporeal True Angels who are The Aspects of Bhall. They transformed into small radiant meteors on the battlefield, immune to dark magic and decimating enemy ranks until they detonate and cause even more damage. Only a small percentage of those that attempt the ritual become possessed by the ifrit, but those that do turn the tides of battle. [PARAGRAPH]In the current age of Church of Bhall are called the Ember Legion. Most of its members are Orcs of the Clan of Embers. They continue to practice self immolation, although the Ifrit rarely take them as hosts or bless them, and are also known to sacrifice captives and their own children to the sacred fires.

When a soul passes from the Bloodfields to the The Temple of Supplication, the chaos is ended. The vault of Aeron was formed to train demons in all the skills they will need on Erebus. It could be thought of as a great academy, but it's closer to say that it is a great temple. Demons learn to fight, lie, and channel power. They learn the great deceptions, and to subjugate themselves to their superiors. Through this training they become a part of the infernal hierarchy. Priests as well as warriors, commanders and soldiers. Many demons are tasked with missions in Erebus as part of this training. Imps are students early in their training. Many of the intelligent demons in Erebus are just in a stage of their training here. Those that have passed beyond this vault are the most rare and powerful of processed souls, demonic lords and princes. [PARAGRAPH]Occasionally particularly vile petitioners (priests of the veil, etc) will skip all the earlier stages and start here in Aeron's vault ready for training. The easiest way to matriculate straight to Aeron's vault, however, is to graduate from the School of Sadism.

The Empyrean was the greatest force for good in the slowly darkening Patria. Though it was devoted to Lugus, the Overcouncil had members from all holy religions. It was the only real force within Patria that could defy the Imprimatur Council;angels stood along the walls of Dies Diei. [PARAGRAPH]Though there had been many plots to try to undermine the city and the overcouncil, none had succeeded. It was the endless night that led to its downfall. [PARAGRAPH]Night strengthened the Aphotic Throne. It strengthened the vampires, werewolves and creatures that the sun forced back into the dark corners of the world. It weakened the angels of Lugus and the priests that were blessed each dawn. [PARAGRAPH]But that is not what led to the fall. It was fear. [PARAGRAPH]The first missed dawn started a panic in Dies Diei. The Overcouncil attempted to advise caution, prayer and communion. But by the third day they were unable to retain control. Horsemen galloped out of the city to invade the Duchy of Dust, who was blamed for all evil things (and often guilty of the charges). People within the city began fighting each other for resources as they feared a coming famine. [PARAGRAPH]Iaegus, Archangel of Shadow, lived on a small farm outside of the city, pretending to be a hermit and apostate. He earned the ire of his neighbors and when they came to confront him they found things they believed were used in dark magic within his home and cellar. [PARAGRAPH]Iaegus was arrested and he didn't stop condemning anyone who got close to him. He screamed at the city as he was dragged through it, and said that they deserved the darkness that was coming for them. Many believed that Iaegus was the one who caused the endless night and he was jailed for binding the sun and cursing the land. [PARAGRAPH]For a brief time the panic in the city subsided and the city turned to blaming Iaegus. The city called for a quick trial, for his condemnation, and his execution. [PARAGRAPH]He remained with the Overcouncil dungeon for three days. Each day the public got more insistent on justice. Each day the sun didn't rise they cried that killing Iaegus was the only way to stop it. [PARAGRAPH]Iaegus received a trial in front of the Overcouncil. It only lasted a single day. By the end the Overcouncil knew the truth, that he was a horrible man, but he wasn't guilty of the crime he had been accused of. He didn't cause the darkness. This truth had always been made known to them in their trials. And they had always followed it. [PARAGRAPH]But the city was unified. Protestors were about to storm the Empyrean and they wanted blood. The Overcounil deliberated, made theories, made excuses. They told themselves that maybe they were being blinded as the sun had been. Maybe he was guilty even though the voice of Lugus within them whispered that it was not so. [PARAGRAPH]They pronounced him guilty. In what would have been the darkest part of night they executed him in the town center. The last look on his face was a smile. In that moment the arda of Lugus was lost and the angels fled from Dies Diei. [PARAGRAPH]Then they stared toward the east and waited for dawn to come. But when it was time, the sun didn't rise. Instead hoofprints sounded through the city. The Riders of Nox Noctis, black and ethereal, charged straight through the walls of the city. Their flashing swords ignored steel and stone and cut easily through flesh. It is not known what happened to the citizens of Dies Diei. It would be years until the gates were opened again, after the sun had returned to Creation, and when it did the city was vacant.

[TAB]The Temple of Temporance is a magnificent basilica standing on the "Ile de la Sheol. " Said to have been the first point of creation, the site has passed back and forth between the control of many nations and many faiths. The current structure was built atop the ruins of temples to every god, and incorporates elements of those ruins to honor each god equally. The grandeur of this architecture is said to be the closest thing to the True Heaven which mortal eyes have ever seen. It is here that the Adjudicators of the Grey Council meet to settle the most serious disputations and issue their most binding decrees.

[TAB]Wyan leads you into the temple of Dagda. Inside you see the pews of a church, but in front of them there is a stand and in front of that seven large thrones on a raised dais. This looks like a place to hold trial and adjudicate, not for sermons.[PARAGRAPH]There are more inquisitors guarding here, a few side chambers, a stairwell leading up to a bell tower and a rectory for the inquisitors to meet to discuss judgements. Wyan leads you past all of these to a back room where a stone staircase leads down into a storage room.[PARAGRAPH]Or what was a storage room. Everything has been cleared out except for two large support pillars. Four inquisitors stand in here, burning incense from their censors and whispering prayers. They circle the fifth figure in the room, who is chained between the pillars.[PARAGRAPH]Bryonna kneels on the stone floor. She is dirty and her hair is thickly matted against her head. Her clothes are a filthy, soiled mess. She does not look up as you enter, and stares down at the floor unmoving. It smells like a nauseating mixture of holy incense and human waste.

The Foxmen are renowned for their Wanderlust. They cannot stand to stay still for very long. They have no settled priesthood or true temples, but there are various shrines in the most remote and dangerous parts of Erebus. It is rarely obvious what makes a site sacred to Tali. Many Foxmen join in on pilgrimages to unique features more sacred to other gods. Some say the destination is completely irrelevant, except as an excuse for adventure. Foxmen tend to avoid crowded cities, but even they will gather at established Trailheads on the outskirts of towns to prepare for long journeys.

The Kuriotates' sprawling city hubs cannot benefit from the City of a Thousand Slums wonder, so they instead get access to the Pixie Gardens. This improves health and happiness, but more importantly it allows the training of Pixies, which are otherwise only be summoned by Mages with Creation Affinity.

[TAB]It lay at the heart of the temple, a strange amalgam of pearl and coral, a thing touched by the power of the Undertow. A living thing, it was constantly rippling, the way a stormy sea ripples, and we could hear its ripples in our minds, the music of distant waves. From the moment when I saw it, I knew I shouldn't have come: but some other part of me rejoiced, drawn to its lure like a moth is drawn to a flame.[PARAGRAPH:1]The priests held gatherings at the beginning of each week, open for all. Newcomers would need to be taken to the chamber with the coral, while the rest of us knew the way, even the ones who'd only been there once before. From the moment we stepped to the surroundings of the temple, we could feel the faint whisper of the waves, guiding us towards the temple's heart. We approached and outsiders always felt unnerved, unable to tell why, only subconsciously noticing the slight wave in our shoulders, our bodies picking up the rhythm of the chamber.[PARAGRAPH:1]We would gather around the coral and dance and laugh and celebrate, seeing strange visions of a vast kingdom, now buried under the sea. As the hours passed, the dance would grow faster and faster and the music would grow louder and louder. Only that the music was only in our heads, an intoxicating storm that was sweeter than any nectar. We were drunk on the coral, ready to do anything, and more than one child was conceived with a total stranger on those nights. Sometimes the priests would join into our celebration, but most of the time they would just stand aside, watching, waiting.[PARAGRAPH:1]The nights always left me exhausted, my body in pain after I had neglected its limits. I worried about going too far-every year, there were some who'd die of the exhaustion-and occasionally I tried to stay away. But the music of the waves would always haunt me in my dreams, a faint tune stuck in my head, infuriatingly just a little too quiet to be heard. And the visions that I would have after a good temple night! I was a poet and an artist, and nothing could leave me more inspired, nothing could compare to the poems I would compose after listening to the corals. Was it more for the sake of myself or my art, I'm not sure, but I always found myself returning after a while.[PARAGRAPH:1]One of the priestesses seemed to take a special interest in me when I returned after an exceptionally long absence. She never said anything, but I could feel her eyes on me when I danced, thoughtful. I would catch the occasional whisper as she discussed something with the others, though I never made out any exact words.[PARAGRAPH:1]After several such nights, something in the music crazed me in a way it had never crazed me before. My dance was wild, my visions feverish, my body screaming in ever-increasing agony as the night progressed. I could see the others growing tired and leaving, but I could not bring myself to stop, could not leave the coral that suddenly seemed to only be singing to me. I could see in the dance of the others that they did not hear the same tune as I did: their rhythm and their steps were all wrong. So when they left I ignored them, knowing that they were deaf to the true music I was hearing.[PARAGRAPH:1]Then, when I was alone save for her, the priestess came and joined my dance. Her dance was perfect, in complete harmony with the waves, and I watched her, enthralled by the beauty I suddenly saw in her. I sought to imitate her elegance, but my own clumsiness was apparent to me-but she did not seem to mind, for she only smiled. She took my hand, and continuing to smile, she led me away from the coral, to a part of the temple I had never been in before. I paid no heed to my surroundings-the ecstasy of the coral was nothing compared to the pleasure of her attention, every muscle in my body shivering each time she looked at me. I was lost in her, the details of her body being like a vast, deep valley I could never climb out of.[PARAGRAPH:1]It never crossed my mind to protest as we came to the pool and she pushed me into the water. I felt something grabbing my arms and legs and pulling me down, but the priestess smiled at me, and her happiness was all that I cared for. I opened my mouth to sing a song of praise for her, and it was only then that I realized I was underwater, water filling my mouth and my lungs. For a brief moment, panic filled me and broke the spell-I screamed, and the priestess only smiled in return.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]The priestess still smiles at me, in a strange amused way that I have a hard time deciphering. It has become hard to think at things, after the drowning. It is much easier to kill, those that the priestess tells me to kill.[PARAGRAPH:1]For a moment, I thought I felt a distant memory when I crushed the skull of the first people the priestess told me to slay. She must have seen my confusion, for she laughed in her angelic voice. With a happy gleam in her eye, she told me that the corpses at my feet were those of my wife and children. I looked at her and the bodies, and there was another momentary feeling of recalling something, but the words bore no meaning to me. I looked at the corpses and shrugged, and we left, her joy echoing in my ears.[PARAGRAPH:1]I'm the bodyguard of the priestess, now. For as long as she is happy with me, the music of the waves will never leave me, and that is all that matters.

[TAB]The Tower of Complacency exerts a powerful mental influence over the citizens of the city that builds it. The people become little more than drones, mindlessly following their Undertow commands. All unhappiness is removed, but the productivity of the city suffers.

[TAB]The Calabim society is a brutal hierarchy, where ancient Vampire aristocrats lord their power over human cattle through the intermediate ranks of Bloodpets, Moroi, the ambitious younger vassals they have Spawned. They care little for the happiness of their subjects, as their [LINK=BUILDING_GOVERNORS_MANOR]Governor's Manors[\\LINK] turn fear and anguish into productivity. Their armies are mostly cannon fodder. Their real strength lies with the few [LINK=PROMOTION_VAMPIRE]Vampiric[\\LINK] officers who take the field. [PARAGRAPH][LINK=PROMOTION_VAMPIRE]Vampiric[\\LINK] units can refresh themselves by [LINK=SPELL_FEED]Feeding[\\LINK] on lesser souls, and gain great power by [LINK=SPELL_FEAST]Feasting[\\LINK] on citizens in their cities. [LINK=UNIT_LOSHA]Losha Valas[\\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_VAMPIRE_LORD]Vampire Lords[\\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_BRUJAH]Brujah[\\LINK], and [LINK=UNIT_BROOD_GUARD]Brood Guards[\\LINK] start with Vampire promotion. Once you have leaned [LINK=TECH_FEUDALISM]Feudalism[\\LINK], living units of at least level 7 (or level 3 if a [LINK=UNIT_MOROI]Moroi[\\LINK] ) may use the [LINK=literal]Gift Vampirism[\\LINK] ability to become vampires. This requires that the unit be in a city with a [LINK=BUILDING_GOVERNORS_MANOR]Governor's Manor[\\LINK] or on the same tile as another Vampire. [PARAGRAPH]Vampires can learn Mage-level magic in the [LINK=BONUS_MANA_BODY]Body[\\LINK], [LINK=BONUS_MANA_DEATH]Undeath[\\LINK], [LINK=BONUS_MANA_MIND]Mind[\\LINK], and [LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]Shadow[\\LINK] spheres. When a new Vampire is Spawned, it may automatically learn such magic as its Sire knew. That includes those spell sphere as well as the [LINK=PROMOTION_ARCANE]Arcane[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_SUMMONER]Summoner[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_SUNDERED]Sundered[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_STIGMATA]Stigmata[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_TWINCAST]Twincast[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_EXTENSION1]Spell Extension I[\\LINK], and [LINK=PROMOTION_EXTENSION2]Spell Extension II[\\LINK] promotions. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Age of Ice almost spelled the end of the vampires. When the vast sheets spread over the once-fertile land, their main source of food, humanity, started to become scarce and ever more concentrated in small tribes. Fearing a fate worse than death-the shadowy almost-death of a vampire deprived of fresh nourishment for centuries-most vampires tried to cling to the ever-shrinking communities of survivors. A lone vampire trapped in a small group of people quickly switches from hunter to prey. One by one, the vampires were dispatched to the afterlife. [PARAGRAPH:1]Of those few vampires who escaped the hunters, most took to a feral existence, living off whatever inferior blood they could scavenge in the wild, preying off the occasional human unfortunate enough to be caught alone. But some wise few realized that the only path to survival lay in making the natural transition from parasite to master. [PARAGRAPH:1]Led by the ancient siblings Alexis and Flauros, a small group of surviving vampires "adopted" a rag-tag tribe of humans. Using their powers as immortals, unaffected by cold, or exhaustion, gifted with incredible vision and speed, they made sure the tribe had plenty of food. And all they asked in return was an endless, expendable resource: A few drops of blood. But a vampire's powers are not restricted to supernatural senses and strength-their great power is in the mind. [PARAGRAPH:1]Slowly but surely, using their natural powers of guile and persuasion, and dangling the "Dark Gift" as bait to lure the best and strongest humans into helping them, the vampires wormed their way to the top of their little society. Few wished to oppose them and risk losing their valuable hunting skills. Those who did had accidents, or simply disappeared. [PARAGRAPH:1]When the humans finally realized what was happening, it was too late. They were trapped in a hellish situation, little more than cattle for a growing class of parasitic nobility, and they had been trapped there of their own free will. [PARAGRAPH:1]Now, Flauros and Alexis are the Grand Prince and Princess of a depraved and hopeless society of bloodpets and slaves, controlled by the Grand Broods, the vampire families that rule each city as their own personal estate farms, living in decadent luxury, and sating their lust for blood at will. The Calabim are the apex of vampire evolution, an abomination that is the natural enemy of all holy nations.

[TAB]The Grigori are the only civilization that gains the powerful Adventurer unit, except from lair exploration or the Foxmen. The Adventurer is a Great Person and Hero that can be upgraded into almost any human unit. The Grigori use these customizable heroes as elite warriors, and they can grow into some of the best units in the game. This is balanced with an inability to gain the benefits of a state religion. [PARAGRAPH:1]Cassiel was an angel in the service of Dagda. He spent the Age of Dragons protecting the men who hid from the might of the warring gods around them. It was his counsel that led Dagda to create and sign the Compact, but Cassiel felt the Compact did not go far enough. He wanted the gods to retreat entirely, to let the men form their own world. When the Compact allowed the gods to battle through men, Cassiel abandoned Dagda's service and began his own crusade to lead men away from a war that has little to do with them. This action gained him few allies among the gods or the humans who serve them. A few brave souls were attracted to Cassiel's creed, though he refused to offer any divine boons or even direct leadership to them. His followers must adhere to his ideas and lead themselves. Throughout the ages the cities of the Grigori offered safe haven for those who wanted to lead their own lives. The wars of the Age of Magic and the scarcity of the Age of Ice took its toll on them like every other land, but they sought help not from the heavens but from themselves. [PARAGRAPH:1]In the Age of Rebirth, Cassiel still stands, offering others ideas and guidance but little more, and some brave few are still drawn to his ideas. Among those who seek asylum in his lands are the Luonnotar, who teach that none of the gods acting on Erebus is worthy of worship, but only one greater god who made them. Cassiel certainly agrees with the first part of this, though he isn't forthcoming on the second.

The Overcouncil is founded when [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\\LINK] is founded. It can only be joined by Neutral or Good players that have researched the Way of the Wise technology. Although they don't have to worship Lugus to join, they can't be members of [LINK=CIVIC_UNDERCOUNCIL]The Undercouncil[\\LINK] or have [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\\LINK] as their state religion. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Being a member of the Overcouncil grants a significant diplomacy bonus with other members. It also forces members to comply with any resolutions that the Overcouncil has voted and agreed on, unless the player wants to defy and leave the Overcouncil. Overall these resolutions can be powerful and restrictive. Players that expect to remain members of the Overcouncil should expect to enjoy the advantages of the friendships it allows, but also be subject to its control. That is unless they maintain the relationships required to be voted the head of the council and get to pick the decrees themselves. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each member of the Overcouncil has one vote on resolutions. Both the Empyrean hero Chalid Astrakein and the Malakim hero Teutorix grant the players that control them an additional vote on the Overcouncil. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Undercouncil is run by money; nearly all of its resolutions cost gold from its members. They can vote to declare war on a common enemy, and open borders to each other. There are no restrictive resolutions on the Undercouncil, they never vote to enforce a civic or outlaw anything but players don't get the larger attitude modifier members of the Overcouncil share with each other. [H1]Alignment[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]There are three alignments in Fall from Heaven, Good, Neutral and Evil. Each leader starts with one and some units and civics can only be used by players of a specific alignment. It also affects your diplomatic relations with other players, granting you bonuses to players of the same alignment and negatives to players of other alignments.[PARAGRAPH:2]The only way to change your alignment is by adopting a State Religion. The Order, Ringgivers, House of Plenty, Unblemished, or Matronae make any player who adopts them good. The Ashen Veil, Ember Legion, Coven, Anointed, Sons of Discord, or White Hand (after The Draw ritual is completed) make any player who adopts them evil. The Grey Council makes any player neutral. The Empyrean, Brotherhood of Wardens, or Runes of Kilmorph make evil players neutral, while leaving good good. The Stewards of Inequity, Council of Esus, or Undertow make good players neutral, while leaving evil playes evil. The Foxmen state religion can cause alignments to change at random.

[H1]Affinity[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Some creatures have affinity for a particular mana type. This means that they gain a strength bonus equal to their affinity amount for each source of that type of mana you control. So a creature that has Nature Affinity: 1 gets +1 for every nature mana you own. A creature with Death Affinity: 2 gets +2 strength for every death mana you control. [PARAGRAPH:2]Affinity may be inherent to a unit or to a promotion. [PARAGRAPH:2]Every Mage is granted an affinity promotion, which not only increases its strength but also grants stronger versions of the usual spells within that sphere. You must have an effective supply of a mana type in order for your arcane units to be gifted affinity in that sphere. The effective supply includes all the sources of real mana you control, plus modifiers unique to each leader, state religion, unit's religion, and whatever is found on the unit's plot. [PARAGRAPH:2]Nearly a quarter of mages, those the Amurites call "Petrarchs," are gifted in 2 spheres. Those gifted in 3 dominions, whom the Amurites call "Decliarchs," are are extremely rare and always powerful. Only Kylorin, who mastered affinity for every precept, has ever shown affinity for more than 3 spheres. [PARAGRAPH:2]With a sufficient mana supply, Disciples may also be granted affinity for their god's dominion. This is less rare for priests, especially high priests, but still not common.

[H1]Ardas[\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The term Arda refers to the divine power that a god is able to grant to his priests and to his angels.[PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Dragons, the gods could grant a full strength arda to anyone they wished, even those fighting deep in enemy territory. The Compact changed things. The gods are now only permitted to extend an arda to their servants in Erebus based on the strength of the faith manifested by their nearby mortal worshippers. [PARAGRAPH]Alliances and enmities between the gods mean that faith in the caster's own religion is not the only relevant factor, as friendly gods may allow the caster's gods some strength and believers in the god's enemies may sheild their neighbors against his attacks. 

[PARAGRAPH] In this modmod the Strength of an Arda is represented by a range of promotion that primarily influence the chance that spells will miscast. Units with a religion and the Divine promotion will have these Arda level promotions autoomatically swapped out based on a number of factors. These include the state religion of the caster's owner, the state religion of the player who controlls the territory on which he unit is located, the preferences of the player's AI towards each religion, the religions present in the nearest city, the religious buildings in the nearest city, the distances from various holy cities, and by Mana or unique features present on the caster's tile or on adjacent tiles.


[PARAGRAPH]All priests have their Ardas weakened by the presence of the Children of the One or of the Matronae in the world, especially in cities nearby. Once the Matronae influence is strong enough, priests in the vicinity of Matronae cities or of Apostates will abdondon their leaders and become Apostates themselves. Once the Children of the One have enough influence, priests may abandon their faith and become rebellious, possibly disbanding themselves of defecting to the Grigori.

It is strenthened near the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_TAPESTRY_HOUSE]Tapestry House[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_PORTAL]Portals[\LINK], [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_HELLFIRE]Hellfire[\LINK], and [LINK=FEATURE_TORMENTED_SOULS]Tormented Souls[\LINK], and weakened on [LINK=FEATURE_HALLOWED_GROUND]Hallowed Ground[\LINK] and [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_RING_OF_WARDING]Rings of Warding[\LINK].

[H1]The Armageddon Counter[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The Armageddon counter goes up when bad things happen (cities are razed, The Ashen Veil is founded, an entropy node is built, etc) and down when good things happen (Mardero dies, The Ashen Veil holy city is razed, etc. ). Depending on the civs in the game the Armageddon Counter either rises slowly over the course of the game, or tends to grow to about 20-40 and then levels off (assuming the player doesn't do anything to influence it). The [LINK=GAMEOPTION_NO_GLOBAL_COUNTER]Hallowed Ground[\\LINK] eliminates the AC from the game. The [LINK=GAMEOPTION_DOUBLE_GLOBAL_COUNTER]Last Days[\\LINK] doubles the rate at which it changes. [PARAGRAPH:2]It affects many things. It controls how many free units are granted by the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\\LINK] [LINK=BUILDING_PLANAR_GATE]Planar Gates[\\LINK], and when various random events will occur. [LINK=CONCEPT_HELL_TERRAIN]Hell Terrain[\\LINK] will only spread to [LINK=CIVILIZATION_INFERNAL]Infernal[\\LINK] territory until the AC is more than 10, at which point it begins to spread to land owned by players with [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\\LINK] as their State Religion. At 25 it may start spreading to other Evil lands, at 30 to unowned lands, at 50 to Neutral lands, and at 90 even to Good lands. The AC also influence the rate at which units with the [LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_DEMON]Demon[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_POSSESSED]Demon Possessed[\\LINK], or [LINK=PROMOTION_KANNAS_WHIP]Kanna's Whip[\\LINK] promotions may spread hell terrain to their tiles. [PARAGRAPH:2]If hell is beginning to creep into your lands you have a few options to respond. Sending out some units to sack The Ashen Veil holy city would be an excellent way to get the Armageddon counter under control and to keep hell out of your lands. You could also gift a few powerful units to a player that is at war with the Infernals if you wanted to contribute without getting into the war directly. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Armageddon counter also influences the chance that fire spreads to nearby tiles and the attitude modifier between good and evil civs. There is a promotion called [LINK=PROMOTION_STIGMATA]Stigmata[\\LINK] that gives the unit a percentage bonus equal to half the Armageddon counter as well as other mechanics that reward some players (especially the Sheaim) for having a high Armageddon count. [PARAGRAPH:2]Since the alignment attitudes are influenced by the Armageddon count (getting better towards their own alignment and worse towards the opposed alignment) when the Armageddon count gets high huge good vs evil battles tend to break out. [PARAGRAPH:2]Kael's Notes: Functionally the AC serves to bring additional conflict to the end game. In Beyond the Sword Firaxis added espionage and corporations to address late game stagnancy. We were trying to solve the same problem but did it with the AC to try to bring conflict and a sense of urgency to the late game.

[H1]Hell Terrain[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Hell Terrain represents the corruption which can spread across Erebus as it falls under the influence of Evil. It is very much tied to the [LINK=CONCEPT_ARMAGEDDON_COUNTER]Armageddon Counter[\\LINK], but its effects are local instead of global. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The [LINK=GAMEOPTION_NO_PLOT_COUNTER]No Hell Terrain[\\LINK] game option prevents the spread of hell entirely. (The [LINK=FEATURE_HALLOWED_GROUND]Hallowed Ground[\\LINK] improvement prevents the spread of hell terrain into the tile, but is only used for scenarios. ) Otherwise, Hell Terrain always spreads quickly into territory held by the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_INFERNAL]Infernals[\\LINK], and recedes from territory held by the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MERCURIANS]Mercurians[\\LINK]. If an adjacent tile (or one the other side of a [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_PORTAL]Portal[\\LINK] ) is already corrupted, then Hell may spread into lands whose owner has [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\\LINK] as a State Religion when the AC more than 10, into lands held by other Evil leaders once the AC passes 25, into the lands of Neutral leaders once it passes 50, and into the lands of Good leaders once it passes 90. It recedes faster from Good lands, slower from Evil lands, and not at all from lands held by The Ashen Veil. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The appearance of [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_HELLFIRE]Hellfire[\\LINK], a [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_NECROTOTEM]Necrototem[\\LINK], or [LINK=FEATURE_TORMENTED_SOULS]Tormented Souls[\\LINK] on a tile turns it into Hell Terrain instantly, and keeps it that way as long as it remains. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MANA_ENTROPY]Entropy Node[\\LINK] may flair up and turn the surrounding tiles into Hell. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Units with the [LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_DEMON]Demon[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_POSSESSED]Demon Possessed[\\LINK], or [LINK=PROMOTION_KANNAS_WHIP]Kanna's Whip[\\LINK] promotions may spread it to the tile they occupy regardless of how pure or tainted adjacent tiles are. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Units with the [LINK=PROMOTION_ANGEL]Angel[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_BLESSED]Blessed[\\LINK], or [LINK=PROMOTION_CROWN_OF_BRILLANCE]Crown of Brilliance[\\LINK] promotions may help to slow or reverse the spread of hell. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The [LINK=SPELL_SANCTIFY]Sanctify[\\LINK] spell and the [LINK=BUILDING_CHANCEL_OF_GUARDIANS]Chancel of the Guardians[\\LINK] building can instantly heal hell terrain. [H1]Puppet States[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Puppet States can be formed when a civilization with knowledge of how to form Vassal States conquers a city. Puppet States are created as a Vassal of the conquering player, and are the same civilization type as the previous city owner. Puppet States are a special type of vassal in that they don't get a Palace and are permanently a Vassal unless they achieve Legitimacy. A Puppet State achieves Legitimacy when it is the last remaining civ of it's civilization type. At that point it becomes a regular Vassal rather than a Puppet State.

[H1]Revolutions[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]This game option allows sections of disgruntled empires to rise up together and demand changes or attempt to break away from the motherland. No matter what the source of the complaint, you will be given an option to either ignore the complaint or accept the cities demands. If their demands go unmet and situations deteriorate, the cities may give you an ultimatum and take up arms if you do not comply![PARAGRAPH:2]HOW IT WORKS:[PARAGRAPH:2]This component is intended to add realistic dynamics to the game, making keeping your cities and regions happy more important and challenging. Each city in your empire will have factors that make it want to stay and factors that make it want to rebel. If you cannot find a balance that keeps each of your cities happy, you will face revolts! Revolts come in many different styles, including requests to change civics, requests to change state religion, and demands for independence. No matter what the scenario, you will always be given choices when confronted with a rebellious city.

[H1]Werewolves[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The creation of the hero Baron Duin Halfmorn introduces the first werewolf to the world and may start an epidemic of lycanthropy. [PARAGRAPH:1]When any Werewolf kills a unit in combat there is a chance the victim will rise as a Ravenous Werewolf under its killer's control. When another unit kills a Werewolf there is also a chance of the winner becoming a Ravenous Werewolf, although the odds are much lower and it would not change owners in this case. [PARAGRAPH:1]The odds of lycanthropy spreading in combat depend on the relative levels of the two units involved. It is also more likely to spread if the Werewolf is Duin than if a Greater Werewolf, if a Greater Werewolf than if a Blooded Werewolf, and if a Blooded Werewolf than if a Ravenous Werewolf. There is no chance of it spreading to units that are not alive, to Animals, to Beasts, or to units with the Immune to Disease, Werewolf Slaying, or Spirit III promotions. [PARAGRAPH:1]Newborn Ravenous Werewolves are dangerous and unpredictable. They start Enraged and so ignore your commands. Unless their owner also controls the Baron, they will start Rebellious and may eventually become Barbarian units. [PARAGRAPH:1]When a Ravenous Werewolf kills a living unit, its rage is sated and it upgrades to a Blooded Werewolf. Blooded Werewolves have a small chance of upgrading to loyal Greater Werewolves when they kill living units. [PARAGRAPH:1]Units that fall to Lycanthropy keep all their promotions, but loose the ability to cast any spells. If you loose a hero to lycanthropy you will not be able to resurrect him until his werewolf self is killed. [PARAGRAPH:1]Baron Duin Halfmorn has a unique ability to dominate other werewolves, converting them to his owner's control. Victims of Lycanthropy will also become loyal to whoever cured them of their curse, which can only be done through the Spirit III spell Assuage. [PARAGRAPH:2]Kael's Notes: This is a double-win mechanic. Meaning that it rewards players who are already winning, increasing the gap between winning and losing players. Although they are difficult to balance double-win mechanics are useful because they reduce the dull grind of chewing through the players that remain in a game if the player has already won, allowing him to steamroll and achieve victory.

[H1]World Spells[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Each civilization was a World Spell they can use. These spells have a huge effect but can only be used once per game so consider carefully before you use them. Of course they help us differentiate each of the civilizations. But we also wanted to add a strategic option where the player was forced to decide when was the best moment to use the ability. As such all of the World Spells generally grow more powerful over time, rewarding players who don't profit from there use early on.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: The Ljosalfar are a defensive civilization-after all, they can't build any siege weapons. Instead, the Light Elves are capable of effectively mounting a war of attrition, using their forested infrastructure to overwhelm the opponent with units and pillage his lands until he's as good as dead. There are alternative methods as well-getting the Baron from the Feral Bond tech and unleashing a horde of Werewolves is an effective way of taking down enemy cities, and mages always exist. With their ability to build things in forests, the Elves have a good synergy with the Fellowship of the Leaves' forest bonuses-but a Fellowship strategy isn't strictly necessary, and following an aggressive religion like the Undertow will give good early attack units in the form of the Drown.
